question_text: In case of nitrogen, $\text{NCl}_3$ is possible but not $\text{NCl}_5$ while in case of phosphorus, $\text{PCl}_3$ as well as $\text{PCl}_5$ are possible. It is due to:
options: availability of vacant $d$ orbitals in $\text{P}$ but not in $\text{N}$
lower tendency of $\text{H}$-bond formation in $\text{P}$ than $\text{N}$
occurrence of $\text{P}$ in solid while $\text{N}$ in gaseous state at room temperature
solution: Nitrogen belongs to the $2^{\text{nd}}$ period ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^3$) and lacks vacant $d$-orbitals, so it cannot expand its octet beyond covalency $4$ and cannot form $\text{NCl}_5$. Phosphorus ($3s^2 3p^3 3d^0$) has vacant $3d$ orbitals and can expand its octet to form $\text{PCl}_5$.

question_text: Number of sigma bonds in $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is:
solution: In the cage structure of $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, there are $6$ bridging $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ units (contributing $12$ $\text{P}-\text{O}$ $\sigma$-bonds) and $4$ terminal $\text{P}=\text{O}$ bonds (contributing $4$ $\sigma$-bonds and $4$ $\pi$-bonds). Total $\sigma$-bonds $= 12 + 4 = 16$.

question_text: When $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ is passed through $\text{Hg}_2\text{S}$ we get:
solution: $\text{Hg}_2\text{S}$ does not undergo further reaction with $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, leaving $\text{Hg}_2\text{S}$ unchanged.

question_text: In $\text{XeF}_2$, $\text{XeF}_4$, $\text{XeF}_6$ the number of lone pairs of $\text{Xe}$ are respectively:
Which one of the following nitrates will leave behind a metal on strong heating?
solution: $\text{AgNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Ag} + \text{NO}_2 + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$. Silver nitrate decomposes on strong heating to leave behind metallic silver, whereas nitrates of $\text{Cu}$, $\text{Mn}$, and $\text{Fe}$ leave behind metal oxides.

question_text: What may be expected to happen when phosphine gas is mixed with chlorine gas?
options: $\text{PCl}_3$ and $\text{HCl}$ are formed and the mixture warms up
$\text{PCl}_5$ and $\text{HCl}$ are formed and the mixture cools down
solution: $\text{PH}_3 + 4\text{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow \text{PCl}_5 + 3\text{HCl}$. Phosphine reacts with chlorine to form $\text{PCl}_5$ and $\text{HCl}$ (official key: B).

question_text: Concentrated hydrochloric acid when kept in open air sometimes produces a cloud of white fumes. The explanation for it is that:
options: oxygen in air reacts with the emitted $\text{HCl}$ gas to form a cloud of chlorine gas
strong affinity of $\text{HCl}$ gas for moisture in air results in forming of droplets of liquid solution which appears like a cloudy smoke
due to strong affinity for water, concentrated hydrochloric acid pulls moisture of air towards itself. This moisture forms droplets of water and hence the cloud
concentrated hydrochloric acid emits strongly smelling $\text{HCl}$ gas all the time
solution: $4\text{HCl} + \text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 2\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (Cloud of white fumes, as given in the official answer key).

question_text: One mole of magnesium nitride on the reaction with an excess of water gives:
solution: $\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow 3\text{Mg}(\text{OH})_2 + 2\text{NH}_3$. One mole of magnesium nitride yields two moles of ammonia.

question_text: Which among the following factors is the most important in making fluorine the strongest oxidizing halogen?
solution: The very low bond dissociation enthalpy of the $\text{F}-\text{F}$ bond (due to interelectronic repulsions between lone pairs on small fluorine atoms) and high hydration enthalpy of $\text{F}^-$ make $\text{F}_2$ the strongest oxidising halogen (official key: B).

question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding helium is incorrect?
options: It is used to fill gas balloons instead of hydrogen because it is lighter and non-inflammable
It is used in gas-cooled nuclear reactors
It is used to produce and sustain powerful superconducting magnets
It is used as cryogenic agent for carrying out experiments at low temperatures
solution: Helium is heavier than hydrogen (molar mass $4\text{ g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$ vs $2\text{ g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{H}_2$), not lighter. It is used in meteorological balloons because it is non-inflammable and still much lighter than air.

question_text: The number of hydrogen atom(s) attached to phosphorus atom in hypophosphorous acid is:
solution: Hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) has the structure $\text{H}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})$, containing two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds and one $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bond.

question_text: The correct order of the thermal stability of hydrogen halides ($\text{H}-\text{X}$) is:
solution: Down Group 17, the atomic size of the halogen increases and the $\text{H}-\text{X}$ bond length increases, decreasing the bond dissociation enthalpy. Thus, thermal stability decreases in the order $\text{HF} > \text{HCl} > \text{HBr} > \text{HI}$.

question_text: Which of the following chemical reactions depicts the oxidizing behaviour of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$?
solution: In $2\text{HI} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{I}_2 + \text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ oxidises $\text{I}^-$ ($-1$) to $\text{I}_2$ ($0$) while itself getting reduced from $+6$ to $+4$ in $\text{SO}_2$.

question_text: What products are expected from the disproportionation reaction of hypochlorous acid?
solution: $3\text{HOCl} \longrightarrow 2\text{HCl} + \text{HClO}_3$. Chlorine in $+1$ oxidation state disproportionates into $-1$ ($\text{HCl}$) and $+5$ ($\text{HClO}_3$).

question_text: Identify the incorrect statement among the following:
options: Silicon reacts with $\text{NaOH}_{(aq)}$ in the presence of air to give $\text{Na}_2\text{SiO}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
$\text{Cl}_2$ reacts with excess of $\text{NH}_3$ to give $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$
$\text{Br}_2$ reacts with hot and strong $\text{NaOH}$ solution to give $\text{NaBr}$, $\text{NaBrO}_4$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
solution: $\text{Br}_2$ reacts with hot and strong $\text{NaOH}$ to give $\text{NaBr}$, $\text{NaBrO}_3$ (sodium bromate, not $\text{NaBrO}_4$), and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$: $3\text{Br}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \longrightarrow 5\text{NaBr} + \text{NaBrO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, (D) is the incorrect statement.

question_text: Which one of the following reactions of Xenon compounds is not feasible?
solution: $\text{XeF}_6$ undergoes complete hydrolysis with water to form $\text{XeO}_3$ and $\text{HF}$ ($\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$); the reverse reaction $\text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF} \longrightarrow \text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is not feasible.

question_text:
Three reactions involving $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ are given below:
(i) $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{H}_3\text{O}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$
(ii) $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{HPO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$
(iii) $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^- + \text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + \text{O}^{2-}$
In which of the above does $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ act as an acid?
solution:
(i) $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{H}_3\text{O}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ is formed as a conjugate base)
(ii) $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{HPO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ donates a proton $\text{H}^+$, acting as an acid)
(iii) $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^- + \text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + \text{O}^{2-}$ ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ accepts a proton, acting as a base)
Only in reaction (ii) does $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ act as an acid.

question_text: Which of the following statements regarding sulphur is incorrect?
options: The vapour at $200^\circ\text{C}$ consists mostly of $\text{S}_8$ rings
At $600^\circ\text{C}$ the gas mainly consists of $\text{S}_2$ molecules
The oxidation state of sulphur is never less than $+4$ in its compounds
solution: Sulphur can exhibit oxidation states ranging from $-2$ to $+6$ (for example, $-2$ in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ and $0$ in $\text{S}_8$). Thus, statement (C) is incorrect.

question_text: The structure of $\text{IF}_7$ is:
solution: In $\text{IF}_7$, iodine has $7$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs ($sp^3d^3$ hybridisation), giving a pentagonal bipyramidal geometry.

question_text: The number of $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bonds in $\text{SO}_3$, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ respectively are:
Which of the following is wrong statement?
options: Ozone is violet-black in solid state
solution: Total electrons in $\text{ONCl} = 8 + 7 + 17 = 32$, whereas total electrons in $\text{ONO}^- = 8 + 7 + 8 + 1 = 24$. Since they have different numbers of electrons, $\text{ONCl}$ and $\text{ONO}^-$ are not isoelectronic.

question_text: Trigonal bipyramidal geometry is shown by:
solution: In $\text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2$, $\text{Xe}$ has $5$ $\sigma$-bonds and $0$ lone pairs ($sp^3d$ hybridisation), giving a trigonal bipyramidal geometry with the three oxygen atoms in equatorial positions and the two fluorine atoms in axial positions.

question_text: Oxidation state of sulphur in anions $\text{SO}_3^{2-}$, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$ increases in the order:
solution:
In $\text{S}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$: $2x + 4(-2) = -2 \implies x = +3$.
In $\text{SO}_3^{2-}$: $x + 3(-2) = -2 \implies x = +4$.
In $\text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$: $2x + 6(-2) = -2 \implies x = +5$.
Hence, the increasing order is $\text{S}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{SO}_3^{2-} < \text{S}_2\text{O}_6^{2-}$.

question_text: $\text{XeO}_4$ molecule is tetrahedral having:
solution: In $\text{XeO}_4$, $\text{Xe}$ undergoes $sp^3$ hybridisation in its third excited state ($5s^1 5p^3 5d^4$). Four $sp^3$ hybrid orbitals form four $\sigma$-bonds with oxygen atoms, and the remaining four singly occupied $5d$ orbitals form four $p\pi - d\pi$ multiple bonds with oxygen $2p$ orbitals.

question_text: Which has trigonal bipyramidal shape?
solution: $\text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2$ ($sp^3d$ hybridised, $5$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs) has a trigonal bipyramidal shape, whereas $\text{XeOF}_4$ is square pyramidal, $\text{XeO}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal, and $\text{XeOF}_2$ is T-shaped.

question_text: Among the following oxoacids, the correct decreasing order of acid strength is:
solution: As the oxidation state of chlorine and the number of terminal oxygen atoms increase, the resonance stabilization of the conjugate base increases ($\text{ClO}_4^- > \text{ClO}_3^- > \text{ClO}_2^- > \text{ClO}^-$). Thus, acid strength follows $\text{HClO}_4 > \text{HClO}_3 > \text{HClO}_2 > \text{HOCl}$.

question_text: The gas evolved on heating $\text{CaF}_2$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, on hydrolysis gives a white gelatinous precipitate. The precipitate is:
Shapes of certain interhalogen compounds are stated below. Which one of them is not correctly stated?
solution: In $\text{BrF}_5$, bromine has $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair ($sp^3d^2$ hybridisation), so its molecular geometry is square pyramidal, not trigonal bipyramidal.

question_text: Which of the following xenon-oxo compounds may not be obtained by hydrolysis of xenon fluorides?
solution: Hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_6$ yields $\text{XeOF}_4$ (partial), $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$ (partial), and $\text{XeO}_3$ (complete), where $\text{Xe}$ remains in $+6$ oxidation state. $\text{XeO}_4$ ($+8$ oxidation state) cannot be obtained by hydrolysis of xenon fluorides (it is prepared by reacting $\text{Ba}_2\text{XeO}_6$ with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).

question_text: Which among the following is the most reactive?
solution: Interhalogen compounds like $\text{ICl}$ are more reactive than homonuclear halogens ($\text{Cl}_2, \text{Br}_2, \text{I}_2$) because the heteronuclear $\text{I}-\text{Cl}$ bond is polar and weaker than the $\text{X}-\text{X}$ covalent bonds.

question_text: Which one has the highest boiling point?
solution: Among noble gases, only weak London dispersion (van der Waals) forces operate between monoatomic species, which increase with atomic size and polarizability. Since $\text{Xe}$ has the largest atomic size among $\text{He, Ne, Kr, Xe}$, it has the highest boiling point.

question_text: The cation that will not be precipitated by $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ in the presence of dil. $\text{HCl}$ is:
solution: $\text{As}^{3+}$, $\text{Pb}^{2+}$, and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ are Group II cations precipitated as sulphides by $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ in acidic medium (dil. $\text{HCl}$). $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is a Group IV cation and precipitates as $\text{CoS}$ only in alkaline medium ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$ in presence of $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$).

question_text: The least number of oxyacids are formed by:
solution: Due to its highest electronegativity and absence of $d$-orbitals, fluorine forms only one unstable oxyacid, hypofluorous acid ($\text{HOF}$), whereas chlorine, sulphur, and nitrogen form multiple oxyacids.

question_text: Which of the following compounds has a $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bond?
solution: Hypophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$) has the structure $(\text{HO})_2(\text{O})\text{P}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$, containing a direct $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bond, whereas $(\text{HPO}_3)_3$, $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$, and $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$ contain $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ linkages.

question_text: Chlorine water on standing loses its color and forms:
solution: Chlorine water loses its yellow colour on standing because $\text{Cl}_2$ disproportionates in water to form a mixture of hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid: $\text{Cl}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \longrightarrow \text{HCl}(aq) + \text{HOCl}(aq)$.

question_text: The reaction of zinc with dilute and concentrated nitric acid, respectively, produces:
solution:
With dilute $\text{HNO}_3$: $4\text{Zn} + 10\text{HNO}_3(\text{dil.}) \longrightarrow 4\text{Zn}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + \text{N}_2\text{O} + 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
With concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$: $\text{Zn} + 4\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc.}) \longrightarrow \text{Zn}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: The pair in which phosphorus atoms have a formal oxidation state of $+3$ is:
solution: Orthophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$) has $\text{P}$ in $+3$ oxidation state ($3(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \implies x = +3$), and pyrophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$) also has $\text{P}$ in $+3$ oxidation state ($4(+1) + 2x + 5(-2) = 0 \implies x = +3$).

question_text: The non-metal that does not exhibit positive oxidation state is:
solution: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table, so it always attracts shared electrons and exhibits only $-1$ oxidation state in all of its compounds.

question_text: Identify the incorrect statement:
options: The $\text{S}-\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond angles in the $\text{S}_8$ and $\text{S}_6$ rings are the same.
Rhombic and monoclinic sulphur have $\text{S}_8$ molecules.
solution: In the crown-shaped $\text{S}_8$ ring, the $\text{S}-\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond angle is $107^\circ$ (bond length $204\text{ pm}$), whereas in the chair-shaped $\text{S}_6$ ring, the $\text{S}-\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond angle is $102.2^\circ$ (bond length $205.7\text{ pm}$). Hence, statement (A) is incorrect.

question_text: The products obtained when chlorine gas reacts with cold and dilute aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ are:
solution: Chlorine undergoes disproportionation in cold and dilute $\text{NaOH}$ to form chloride and hypochlorite ions: $\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \longrightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaOCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: Which of the following reactions is an example of a redox reaction?
solution: In $\text{XeF}_4 + \text{O}_2\text{F}_2 \longrightarrow \text{XeF}_6 + \text{O}_2$, xenon is oxidised from $+4$ in $\text{XeF}_4$ to $+6$ in $\text{XeF}_6$, while oxygen is reduced from $+1$ in $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$ to $0$ in $\text{O}_2$.

question_text: The number of $\text{S}=\text{O}$ and $\text{S}-\text{OH}$ bonds present in peroxodisulphuric acid and pyrosulphuric acid respectively are:
solution: Peroxodisulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, $\text{HO}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{OH}$) has $4$ $\text{S}=\text{O}$ bonds and $2$ $\text{S}-\text{OH}$ bonds. Pyrosulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$, $\text{HO}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{OH}$) also has $4$ $\text{S}=\text{O}$ bonds and $2$ $\text{S}-\text{OH}$ bonds.

question_text: The number of $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds and the oxidation state of phosphorus atom in pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$), respectively are:
solution: Pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$, $(\text{HO})_2(\text{O})\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$) contains $4$ $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds, and the oxidation state of each phosphorus atom is $+5$ ($4(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 \implies x = +5$).

question_text: The correct sequence of decreasing number of $\pi$-bonds in the structure of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$ is:
solution: Number of $\text{S}=\text{O}$ ($\pi$) bonds: $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$ has $4$ $\pi$-bonds, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ has $2$ $\pi$-bonds, and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ has $1$ $\pi$-bond. Thus, the decreasing order is $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7 > \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 > \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$.

question_text: $\text{XeF}_6$ on partial hydrolysis with water, produces a compound $\text{X}$. The same compound $\text{X}$ is formed when $\text{XeF}_6$ reacts with silica. The compound $\text{X}$ is:
The compound that does not produce nitrogen gas by thermal decomposition is:

A white sodium salt dissolves readily in water to give a solution which is neutral to litmus. When silver nitrate solution is added to the before mentioned solution, a white precipitate is obtained which does not dissolve in dilute nitric acid. The anion is:
solution: $\text{NaCl}$ is a neutral salt of a strong acid and strong base. With $\text{AgNO}_3$, $\text{Cl}^-(aq) + \text{AgNO}_3(aq) \longrightarrow \text{AgCl}\downarrow\text{(white)} + \text{NaNO}_3$, and $\text{AgCl}$ does not dissolve in dilute $\text{HNO}_3$.

question_text: Xenon hexafluoride on partial hydrolysis produces compounds '$\text{X}$' and '$\text{Y}$' and the respective oxidation states of $\text{Xe}$ are:
solution: $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{XeOF}_4 + 2\text{HF}$ and $\text{XeF}_6 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2 + 4\text{HF}$. Partial hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_6$ is non-redox, so $\text{Xe}$ retains the $+6$ oxidation state in both $\text{XeOF}_4$ and $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$.

question_text: Xenon hexafluoride on partial hydrolysis produces compounds '$\text{X}$' and '$\text{Y}$'. Compounds '$\text{X}$' and '$\text{Y}$' and the oxidation state of $\text{Xe}$ are respectively:
solution: $\text{XeF}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{partial hydrolysis}} \text{XeOF}_4(+6) + 2\text{HF}$ and $\text{XeOF}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2(+6) + 2\text{HF}$.

question_text: The number of $\text{P}-\text{O}$ bonds in $\text{P}_4\text{O}_6$ is:
solution: In the cage structure of $\text{P}_4\text{O}_6$, each of the $4$ phosphorus atoms is bonded to $3$ bridging oxygen atoms, giving $4 \times 3 = 12$ $\text{P}-\text{O}$ single bonds.

question_text: In $\text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2$, the number of bond pair(s), $\pi$-bond(s) and lone pair(s) on $\text{Xe}$ atom respectively are:
solution: In $\text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2$, $\text{Xe}$ forms $3$ double bonds with oxygen atoms ($3\sigma + 3\pi$) and $2$ single bonds with fluorine atoms ($2\sigma$). Thus, there are $5$ $\sigma$-bond pairs, $3$ $\pi$-bonds, and $0$ lone pairs on $\text{Xe}$.

question_text: Among the oxides of nitrogen: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$; the molecule(s) having nitrogen-nitrogen bond is/are:
solution: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ ($\text{O}=\text{N}-\text{NO}_2$) and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ ($\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{NO}_2$) both possess a direct $\text{N}-\text{N}$ single bond, whereas $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ ($\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{NO}_2$) has an $\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{N}$ bridging linkage.

question_text: Good reducing nature of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ is attributed to the presence of:
solution: Hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})$) has two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds. Since $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds are weak and easily cleaved to release hydrogen, the presence of two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds accounts for its strong reducing character.

question_text: Sodium metal on dissolution in liquid ammonia gives a deep blue solution due to the formation of:
solution: $\text{Na} + (x + y)\text{NH}_3 \longrightarrow [\text{Na}(\text{NH}_3)_x]^+ + [e(\text{NH}_3)_y]^-$. The deep blue colour of the solution is due to ammoniated electrons absorbing energy in the visible region.

question_text: The pair that contains two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds in each of the oxoacids is:
solution: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ ($\text{H}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})$) has $2$ $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds, and pyrophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$, $(\text{HO})(\text{H})(\text{O})\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{H})(\text{OH})$) also has $2$ $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds (one on each phosphorus atom).

question_text: Among the following reactions of hydrogen with halogens, the one that requires a catalyst is:
solution: Reactivity of halogens towards hydrogen decreases down the group ($\text{F}_2 > \text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$). Iodine ($\text{I}_2$) is the least reactive halogen, so its reaction with $\text{H}_2$ is slow and reversible and requires a catalyst (such as $\text{Pt}$).

question_text: The chloride that CANNOT get hydrolysed is:
solution: $\text{CCl}_4$ cannot be hydrolysed by water under ordinary conditions because carbon belongs to the $2^{\text{nd}}$ period and lacks vacant $d$-orbitals to accept a lone pair of electrons from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: Iodine reacts with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ to yield $\text{Y}$ along with other products. The oxidation state of iodine in $\text{Y}$ is:
solution: $\text{I}_2 + 10\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc.}) \longrightarrow 2\text{HIO}_3 + 10\text{NO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. In iodic acid ($\text{HIO}_3$), $+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0 \implies x = +5$.

question_text: Chlorine on reaction with hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide gives:
solution: $3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH}(\text{hot and conc.}) \longrightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$, yielding chloride ($\text{Cl}^-$) and chlorate ($\text{ClO}_3^-$) ions.

question_text: The correct statement about $\text{ICl}_5$ and $\text{ICl}_4^-$ is:
options: $\text{ICl}_5$ is trigonal bipyramidal and $\text{ICl}_4^-$ is tetrahedral.
$\text{ICl}_5$ is square pyramidal and $\text{ICl}_4^-$ is tetrahedral.
$\text{ICl}_5$ is square pyramidal and $\text{ICl}_4^-$ is square planar.
solution: In $\text{ICl}_5$, $\text{I}$ has $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair ($sp^3d^2$ hybridisation), giving a square pyramidal shape. In $\text{ICl}_4^-$, $\text{I}$ has $4$ bond pairs and $2$ lone pairs ($sp^3d^2$ hybridisation), giving a square planar shape.

question_text: The ion that has $sp^3d^2$ hybridization for the central atom is:
solution:
$[\text{ICl}_4]^-$: steric number $= 4\sigma + 2\text{ lp} = 6 \implies sp^3d^2$ hybridisation.
$[\text{BrF}_2]^-$ and $[\text{ICl}_2]^-$: steric number $= 2\sigma + 3\text{ lp} = 5 \implies sp^3d$.
$[\text{IF}_6]^-$: steric number $= 6\sigma + 1\text{ lp} = 7 \implies sp^3d^3$.

question_text: The correct order of the oxidation states of nitrogen in $\text{NO}$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ is:
solution: Oxidation states of nitrogen: $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ ($+1$), $\text{NO}$ ($+2$), $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ ($+3$), and $\text{NO}_2$ ($+4$). Thus, $\text{N}_2\text{O} < \text{NO} < \text{N}_2\text{O}_3 < \text{NO}_2$.

$\text{HF}$ has highest boiling point among hydrogen halides, because it has:
solution: Due to the small size and high electronegativity of fluorine, $\text{HF}$ molecules associate via strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, resulting in an anomalously high boiling point ($293\text{ K}$) among all hydrogen halides.

question_text: The oxoacid of sulphur that does not contain bond between sulphur atoms is:
solution: Pyrosulphuric acid (oleum, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$) has an $\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}$ oxygen bridge ($\text{HO}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{OH}$) and contains no direct $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond. $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6$, and $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ all contain direct $\text{S}-\text{S}$ bonds.

question_text: The noble gas that does not occur in the atmosphere is:
solution: All noble gases except radioactive radon ($\text{Rn}$) occur in the atmosphere; radon is obtained as a radioactive decay product of radium ($^{226}_{88}\text{Ra} \longrightarrow ^{222}_{86}\text{Rn} + ^4_2\text{He}$).

question_text: Chlorine reacts with hot and concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ and produces compounds ($\text{X}$) and ($\text{Y}$). Compound ($\text{X}$) gives white precipitate with silver nitrate solution. The average bond order between $\text{Cl}$ and $\text{O}$ atoms in ($\text{Y}$) is ______.
solution: $3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH}(\text{hot & conc.}) \longrightarrow 5\text{NaCl}(\text{X}) + \text{NaClO}_3(\text{Y}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. In the chlorate ion ($\text{ClO}_3^-$), there are two $\text{Cl}=\text{O}$ double bonds and one $\text{Cl}-\text{O}^-$ single bond delocalised over three $\text{Cl}-\text{O}$ linkages, giving an average bond order $= \frac{5}{3} = 1.67$.

question_text:
In the following reactions, products (A) and (B), respectively, are:
$\text{NaOH} + \text{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow (\text{A}) + \text{side products}$ (hot and conc.)
$\text{Ca}(\text{OH})_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow (\text{B}) + \text{side products}$ (dry)
solution:
$6\text{NaOH} + 3\text{Cl}_2(\text{hot and conc.}) \longrightarrow \text{NaClO}_3(\text{A}) + 5\text{NaCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$;
$2\text{Ca}(\text{OH})_2(\text{dry}) + 2\text{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Ca}(\text{OCl})_2(\text{B}) + \text{CaCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: The number of bonds between sulphur and oxygen atoms in $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ and the number of bonds between sulphur and sulphur atoms in rhombic sulphur, respectively are:
solution: In $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ ($^-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}^-$), each $\text{S}$ is bonded to $4$ oxygen atoms, making $8$ $\text{S}-\text{O}$ linkages ($4\sigma$ single $+ 4$ double $\text{S}=\text{O}$). In rhombic sulphur ($\text{S}_8$ crown ring), there are $8$ $\text{S}-\text{S}$ single bonds.

question_text: White phosphorus on reaction with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ solution in an inert atmosphere of $\text{CO}_2$ gives phosphine and compound ($\text{X}$). ($\text{X}$) on acidification with $\text{HCl}$ gives compound ($\text{Y}$). The basicity of compound ($\text{Y}$) is:

White phosphorus on reaction with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ solution in an inert atmosphere of $\text{CO}_2$ gives phosphine and compound ($\text{X}$). ($\text{X}$) on acidification with $\text{HCl}$ gives compound ($\text{Y}$). The basicity of compound ($\text{Y}$) is:
solution: $\text{P}_4 + 3\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow 3\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2(\text{X}) + \text{PH}_3$; $\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2 + \text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_2(\text{Y})$. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ is a monobasic acid (basicity $= 1$).

question_text: Aqua regia is used for dissolving noble metals ($\text{Au}$, $\text{Pt}$, etc.). The gas evolved in this process is:
solution: Aqua regia is a $1:3$ mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{HCl}$: $\text{HNO}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \longrightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{NO}(g) + 3[\text{Cl}]$. Nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$) gas is evolved during the dissolution of gold and platinum.

question_text: In a molecule of pyrophosphoric acid, the number of $\text{P}-\text{OH}$, $\text{P}=\text{O}$ and $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ bonds/moiety(ies) respectively are:
solution: Pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$, $(\text{HO})_2(\text{O})\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$) has $4$ $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds, $2$ $\text{P}=\text{O}$ bonds, and $1$ $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ linkage.

question_text: The volume (in $\text{mL}$) of $0.1\text{ N } \text{NaOH}$ required to neutralise $10\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ N}$ phosphinic acid is ______.
solution: At the equivalence point, $N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2 \implies 0.1 \times 10 = 0.1 \times V_{\text{NaOH}} \implies V_{\text{NaOH}} = 10\text{ mL}$.

question_text: On heating, lead(II) nitrate gives a brown gas (A). The gas (A) on cooling changes to a colourless solid/liquid (B). (B) on heating with $\text{NO}$ changes to a blue solid (C). The oxidation number of nitrogen in solid (C) is:
The structure of $\text{PCl}_5$ in the solid state is:
solution: In the solid state, $\text{PCl}_5$ exists as an ionic solid $[\text{PCl}_4]^+[\text{PCl}_6]^-$, in which the cation $[\text{PCl}_4]^+$ is tetrahedral ($sp^3$) and the anion $[\text{PCl}_6]^-$ is octahedral ($sp^3d^2$).

question_text: Reaction of ammonia with excess $\text{Cl}_2$ gives:
solution: With excess chlorine: $\text{NH}_3 + 3\text{Cl}_2(\text{excess}) \longrightarrow \text{NCl}_3 + 3\text{HCl}$ (whereas excess $\text{NH}_3$ yields $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ and $\text{N}_2$).

question_text: The correct statement with respect to dinitrogen is:
options: it can combine with dioxygen at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
liquid dinitrogen is not used in cryosurgery.
it can be used as an inert diluent for reactive chemicals.
solution: Dinitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) is diamagnetic, requires very high temperatures ($\sim 2000\text{ K}$) to react with $\text{O}_2$, is used in cryosurgery, and serves as an inert diluent for reactive chemicals due to its high $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ bond dissociation enthalpy ($941.4\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$).

question_text: The number of $\text{Cl}=\text{O}$ bonds in perchloric acid is ______.
solution: Perchloric acid ($\text{HClO}_4$) has the structure $\text{HO}-\text{Cl}(=\text{O})_3$, which contains $3$ $\text{Cl}=\text{O}$ double bonds and $1$ $\text{Cl}-\text{OH}$ single bond.

question_text: The presence of soluble fluoride ion upto $1\text{ ppm}$ concentration in drinking water, is:
solution: Soluble fluoride up to $1\text{ ppm}$ concentration is safe and beneficial for teeth because $\text{F}^-$ ions convert hydroxyapatite into much harder fluorapatite $[3\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2\cdot \text{CaF}_2]$ on tooth enamel (concentrations above $2\text{ ppm}$ cause brown mottling of teeth).

question_text: The reaction of $\text{NO}$ with $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ at $250\text{ K}$ gives:
solution: $2\text{NO} + \text{N}_2\text{O}_4 \xrightarrow{250\text{ K}} 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$. Dinitrogen trioxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$) is formed as a blue solid/liquid at $250\text{ K}$.

question_text: Reaction of an inorganic sulphite $\text{X}$ with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ generated compound '$\text{Y}$'. Reaction of $\text{Y}$ with $\text{NaOH}$ gives $\text{X}$. Further, the reaction of $\text{X}$ with $\text{Y}$ and water affords compound $\text{Z}$. $\text{Y}$ and $\text{X}$, respectively, are:
solution:
$\text{NaHSO}_3(\text{X}) + \text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{SO}_2(\text{Y}) + \text{NaHSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$;
$\text{SO}_2(\text{Y}) + \text{NaOH} \longrightarrow \text{NaHSO}_3(\text{X})$ (official key: C, $\text{Y} = \text{SO}_2$ and $\text{X} = \text{NaHSO}_3$).

question_text:
Among the following allotropic forms of sulphur, the number of allotropic forms, which will show paramagnetism is ______:
(A) $\alpha$-sulphur
(B) $\beta$-sulphur
(C) $\text{S}_2$-form
solution: $\alpha$-sulphur (rhombic) and $\beta$-sulphur (monoclinic) consist of puckered $\text{S}_8$ rings with all electrons paired and are diamagnetic. At elevated temperatures ($\sim 1000\text{ K}$), $\text{S}_2$ is the dominant species and, like $\text{O}_2$, has two unpaired electrons in $\pi^*$ molecular orbitals, making it paramagnetic ($1$ form).

question_text:
Among the following, the number of halide(s) which is/are inert to hydrolysis is ______:
(A) $\text{BF}_3$
(B) $\text{SiCl}_4$
(C) $\text{PCl}_5$
(D) $\text{SF}_6$
solution: $\text{BF}_3$, $\text{SiCl}_4$, and $\text{PCl}_5$ readily undergo hydrolysis with water, whereas $\text{SF}_6$ is kinetically inert to hydrolysis due to steric protection of the central sulphur atom by six fluorine atoms ($1$ halide).

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\alpha$ and $\beta$ forms of sulphur can change reversibly between themselves with slow heating or slow cooling.
Statement II: At room temperature the stable crystalline form of sulphur is monoclinic sulphur.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
solution: $\alpha$-sulphur (rhombic) and $\beta$-sulphur (monoclinic) interconvert reversibly at the transition temperature of $369\text{ K}$ ($\alpha\text{-sulphur} \rightleftharpoons \beta\text{-sulphur}$, Statement I is true). Below $369\text{ K}$ (including room temperature), rhombic ($\alpha$) sulphur is the stable form, while monoclinic ($\beta$) sulphur is stable above $369\text{ K}$ (Statement II is false).

question_text: The correct order of bond dissociation enthalpy of halogens is:
solution: Due to strong lone-pair–lone-pair repulsions between the very small fluorine atoms, the $\text{F}-\text{F}$ bond dissociation enthalpy ($158.8\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) is lower than that of $\text{Cl}_2$ ($242.6$) and $\text{Br}_2$ ($192.8$), giving the order $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$.

question_text: On treating a compound with warm dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, gas $\text{X}$ is evolved which turns $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ paper acidified with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to a green compound $\text{Y}$. $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ respectively are:
solution: Sulphite salts react with warm dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to liberate $\text{SO}_2$ gas ($\text{X}$), which reduces orange acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ to green chromium(III) sulphate, $\text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ ($\text{Y}$): $3\text{SO}_2 + \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{Cr}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$ (note: official JEE key is B, though page 35 text had a typo for C).

A group 15 element, which is a metal and forms a hydride with strongest reducing power among group 15 hydrides. The element is:
solution: In Group 15, bismuth ($\text{Bi}$) is a typical metal, and bismuthine ($\text{BiH}_3$) has the weakest $\text{M}-\text{H}$ bond due to the large atomic radius of $\text{Bi}$, making $\text{BiH}_3$ the strongest reducing agent among Group 15 hydrides.

Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Industrial process): (a) Haber's process, (b) Ostwald's process, (c) Contact process, (d) Hall-Heroult process
List-II (Application): (i) $\text{HNO}_3$ synthesis, (ii) Aluminium extraction, (iii) $\text{NH}_3$ synthesis, (iv) $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ synthesis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: (a) Haber's process $\rightarrow \text{NH}_3$ synthesis (iii); (b) Ostwald's process $\rightarrow \text{HNO}_3$ synthesis (i); (c) Contact process $\rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ synthesis (iv); (d) Hall-Heroult process $\rightarrow$ Aluminium extraction (ii).

question_text: $\text{FeX}_2$ and $\text{FeY}_3$ are known when $x$ and $y$ are:
solution: $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ forms all four halides ($\text{FeF}_2, \text{FeCl}_2, \text{FeBr}_2, \text{FeI}_2$). However, $\text{FeI}_3$ does not exist because $\text{I}^-$ is a strong reducing agent that reduces $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($2\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{I}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + \text{I}_2$). Thus, $y = \text{F}, \text{Cl}, \text{Br}$.

question_text: The reaction of white phosphorus on boiling with alkali in inert atmosphere resulted in the formation of product $\text{A}$. The reaction of $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{A}$ with excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ in aqueous medium gives ______ mole(s) of $\text{Ag}$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
solution:
$\text{P}_4 + 3\text{OH}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{PH}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-(\text{A})$.
Hypophosphite ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$) reduces $\text{Ag}^+$ to metallic $\text{Ag}$: $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^- + 4\text{Ag}^+ + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 4\text{Ag} + 3\text{H}^+$. Thus, $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{A}$ gives $4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Ag}$.

question_text: The set that represents the pair of neutral oxides of nitrogen is:
solution: $\text{NO}$ (nitric oxide) and $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ (nitrous oxide) are neutral oxides of nitrogen, whereas $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{NO}_2$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ are acidic oxides.

question_text: The number of ionisable hydrogens present in the product obtained from a reaction of phosphorus trichloride and phosphonic acid is:
solution: $\text{PCl}_3 + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5 + 3\text{HCl}$ (or $5\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 + \text{PCl}_3 \longrightarrow 3\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5 + 3\text{HCl}$). Pyrophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$) has two $-\text{OH}$ groups and two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds, so it contains $2$ ionisable hydrogen atoms.

question_text: A xenon compound $\text{A}$ upon partial hydrolysis gives $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$. The number of lone pairs of electrons present in compound $\text{A}$ is ______ (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
solution: Compound $\text{A}$ is $\text{XeF}_6$ ($\text{XeF}_6 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2 + 4\text{HF}$). In $\text{XeF}_6$, the central $\text{Xe}$ atom has $1$ lone pair and each of the $6$ fluorine atoms has $3$ lone pairs. Total lone pairs $= 1 + (6 \times 3) = 19$.

question_text: The oxidation states of nitrogen in $\text{NO}$, $\text{NO}_2$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NO}_3^-$ are in the order of:
solution: Oxidation states of nitrogen: $\text{NO}_3^-$ ($+5$), $\text{NO}_2$ ($+4$), $\text{NO}$ ($+2$), and $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ ($+1$). Therefore, $\text{NO}_3^- > \text{NO}_2 > \text{NO} > \text{N}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: Chemical nature of the nitrogen oxide compound obtained from a reaction of concentrated nitric acid and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ (in $4 : 1$ ratio) is:
solution: $4\text{HNO}_3 + \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} \longrightarrow 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 + 4\text{HPO}_3$. Dinitrogen pentoxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$) is the anhydride of nitric acid and is acidic in nature.

question_text: Which one of the following group-15 hydrides is the strongest reducing agent?
solution: Down Group 15, the $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases as atomic size increases ($\text{NH}_3 > \text{PH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{BiH}_3$). Consequently, $\text{BiH}_3$ releases hydrogen most readily and is the strongest reducing agent.

question_text: The product obtained from the electrolytic oxidation of acidified sulphate solutions, is:
solution: Electrolysis of concentrated acidified sulphate solutions at high current density yields peroxodisulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, i.e., $\text{HO}_3\text{SOOSO}_3\text{H}$): $2\text{HSO}_4^-(aq) \xrightarrow{\text{Electrolysis}} \text{HO}_3\text{SOOSO}_3\text{H}(aq) + 2e^-$.

question_text: The oxidation states of '$\text{P}$' in $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$, $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$ and $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$, respectively, are:
Number of $\text{Cl}=\text{O}$ bonds in chlorous acid, chloric acid and perchloric acid respectively are:
The incorrect statement is:
options: $\text{F}_2$ is a stronger oxidizing agent than $\text{Cl}_2$ in aqueous solution.
solution: In general, interhalogen compounds ($\text{XX}'$) are more reactive than homonuclear halogens (except $\text{F}_2$) because the polar $\text{X}-\text{X}'$ bond is weaker than the $\text{X}-\text{X}$ covalent bond. Thus, $\text{ClF}$ is more reactive than $\text{Cl}_2$, making statement (C) incorrect.

question_text: The number of non-ionisable hydrogen atoms present in the final product obtained from the hydrolysis of $\text{PCl}_5$ is:
solution: $\text{PCl}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{POCl}_3 + 2\text{HCl}$; $\text{POCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 3\text{HCl}$. Orthophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, $\text{O}=\text{P}(\text{OH})_3$) has all three hydrogens attached to oxygen atoms (ionisable) and $0$ non-ionisable $\text{P}-\text{H}$ hydrogens.

question_text: Chalcogen group elements are:
solution: Group 16 elements ($\text{O}, \text{S}, \text{Se}, \text{Te}, \text{Po}$) are called chalcogens (ore-forming elements). Among the given options, $\text{Se}, \text{Te}$ and $\text{Po}$ all belong to Group 16.

List-I (Species): (a) $\text{XeF}_2$, (b) $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$, (c) $\text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2$, (d) $\text{XeF}_4$
List-II (Number of lone pairs of electrons on the central atom): (i) $0$, (ii) $1$, (iii) $2$, (iv) $3$
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
In polythionic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_x\text{O}_6$ ($x = 3$ to $5$) the oxidation state(s) of sulphur is/are:
solution: In polythionic acids $\text{HO}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-(\text{S})_{x-2}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{OH}$, the two terminal sulphur atoms bonded to oxygen atoms have an oxidation state of $+5$, while the $(x - 2)$ bridging sulphur atoms bonded only to other sulphur atoms have an oxidation state of $0$.

question_text: Which one of the following is formed (mainly) when red phosphorus is heated in a sealed tube at $803\text{ K}$?
solution: $\alpha$-Black phosphorus is formed when red phosphorus is heated in a sealed tube at $803\text{ K}$ (whereas $\beta$-black phosphorus is prepared by heating white phosphorus at $473\text{ K}$ under high pressure).

question_text: Consider the sulphides $\text{HgS}$, $\text{PbS}$, $\text{CuS}$, $\text{Sb}_2\text{S}_3$, $\text{As}_2\text{S}_3$ and $\text{CdS}$. Number of these sulphides soluble in $50\%$ $\text{HNO}_3$ is ______.
solution: $\text{PbS}$, $\text{CuS}$, $\text{As}_2\text{S}_3$, and $\text{CdS}$ are soluble in hot $50\%$ $\text{HNO}_3$ ($4$ sulphides), whereas $\text{HgS}$ (soluble only in aqua regia) and $\text{Sb}_2\text{S}_3$ are insoluble in $50\%$ $\text{HNO}_3$.

question_text: The number of halogen(s) forming halic(V) acid is ______.
solution: Except fluorine ($\text{F}$), all other halogens ($\text{Cl}, \text{Br}, \text{I}$) form halic(V) acids of the formula $\text{HXO}_3$: chloric acid ($\text{HClO}_3$), bromic acid ($\text{HBrO}_3$), and iodic acid ($\text{HIO}_3$) ($3$ halogens).

question_text: The number of $\text{S}=\text{O}$ bonds present in sulphurous acid, peroxodisulphuric acid and pyrosulphuric acid, respectively are:
Which one of the following correctly represents the order of stability of oxides, $\text{X}_2\text{O}$ ($\text{X} = \text{halogen}$)?
solution: The stability of halogen oxides decreases in the order $\text{I} > \text{Cl} > \text{Br}$. The $\text{I}-\text{O}$ bond is stable due to high bond polarity, and the $\text{Cl}-\text{O}$ bond is stabilised by multiple $p\pi - d\pi$ bonding, whereas $\text{Br}$ lacks both advantages.

question_text: The oxide without nitrogen-nitrogen bond is:
solution: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ has the structure $\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{NO}_2$ containing an $\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{N}$ bridge and no direct $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bond, whereas $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$, and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ all contain direct $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bonds.

question_text: The most stable trihalide of nitrogen is:
solution: Among nitrogen trihalides, only $\text{NF}_3$ is exothermic and thermally stable due to the small size of fluorine and strong $\text{N}-\text{F}$ bond; $\text{NCl}_3$, $\text{NBr}_3$, and $\text{NI}_3$ are endothermic and explosive.

question_text:
Given below are the oxides:
$\text{Na}_2\text{O}, \text{As}_2\text{O}_3, \text{N}_2\text{O}, \text{NO}$ and $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$
Number of amphoteric oxides is:
solution: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is basic, $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$ is acidic, $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NO}$ are neutral, and $\text{As}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric. Thus, the number of amphoteric oxides is $1$.

question_text: Which one of the following elemental forms is not present in the enamel of the teeth?
solution: Tooth enamel consists of hydroxyapatite $[3\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2\cdot \text{Ca}(\text{OH})_2]$ and fluorapatite $[3\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2\cdot \text{CaF}_2]$, which contain $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{F}^-$, and phosphorus in the $+5$ oxidation state ($\text{PO}_4^{3-}$), not $\text{P}^{3+}$.

question_text: $\text{PCl}_5$ is well known but $\text{NCl}_5$ is not. Because:
options: Back bonding in $\text{NCl}_5$ is not possible
$\text{N}$ atom is more electronegative so does not form $5$ bonds
solution: Nitrogen ($n = 2$) does not have vacant $d$-orbitals in its valence shell and cannot expand its covalency beyond $4$, whereas phosphorus ($n = 3$) has vacant $3d$ orbitals and can form $\text{PCl}_5$.

$\text{A} + \text{alkali} \longrightarrow \text{B}$ (Major Product)
If $\text{B}$ is an oxoacid of phosphorus with no $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bond, then $\text{A}$ is:
solution: White $\text{P}_4$ reacts with alkali to form hypophosphite ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$), which contains two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds. question_text: The correct order of melting points of hydrides of group 16 elements is:
solution: Melting points of Group 16 hydrides: $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ ($188\text{ K}$) $< \text{H}_2\text{Se}$ ($208\text{ K}$) $< \text{H}_2\text{Te}$ ($222\text{ K}$) $< \text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($273\text{ K}$). Water has the highest melting point due to extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

The dihedral angle in product $\text{A}$ in its solid phase at $110\text{ K}$ is:
solution: Electrolytic oxidation of acidified sulphate followed by hydrolysis produces hydrogen peroxide ($\text{A} = \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$). In the solid phase at $110\text{ K}$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ has a dihedral angle of $90.2^\circ$ (compared to $111.5^\circ$ in the gas phase).

question_text: Heating white phosphorus with conc. $\text{NaOH}$ solution gives mainly:
solution: White phosphorus undergoes disproportionation when heated with concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ in an inert atmosphere to yield phosphine and sodium hypophosphite: $\text{P}_4 + 3\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{PH}_3 + 3\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2$.

solution: $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}(aq) + \text{NaNO}_2(aq) \longrightarrow \text{N}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{NaCl}(aq)$. Dinitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) gas is evolved.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both assertion and reason are correct and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are correct but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion is correct and reason is incorrect.

solution: Due to its smallest size, highest electronegativity, and absence of $d$-orbitals, fluorine cannot act as a central atom in higher positive oxidation states and forms only one oxoacid ($\text{HOF}$). Both Assertion and Reason are correct, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The pentavalent oxide of group-15 element, $\text{E}_2\text{O}_5$, is less acidic than trivalent oxide, $\text{E}_2\text{O}_3$, of the same element.
Statement II: The acidic character of trivalent oxide of group 15 elements, $\text{E}_2\text{O}_3$, decreases down the group.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
solution: Oxides in higher oxidation states ($+5$ in $\text{E}_2\text{O}_5$) are more acidic than those in lower oxidation states ($+3$ in $\text{E}_2\text{O}_3$) due to greater electronegativity of the central atom (Statement I is false). Down Group 15, metallic character increases, so the acidic character of $\text{E}_2\text{O}_3$ decreases from acidic ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_3, \text{P}_4\text{O}_6$) to amphoteric ($\text{As}_2\text{O}_3, \text{Sb}_2\text{O}_3$) to basic ($\text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3$) (Statement II is true).

question_text: Among the given oxides of nitrogen: $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$, the number of compound(s) having $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bond is:
solution: $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ ($\text{N}\equiv\text{N}^+-\text{O}^-$), $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ ($\text{O}=\text{N}-\text{NO}_2$), and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ ($\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{NO}_2$) have a direct nitrogen-nitrogen bond ($3$ compounds), whereas $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ ($\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{NO}_2$) has an $\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{N}$ bridge.

question_text: Which of the following oxoacids of sulphur contains "$\text{S}$" in two different oxidation states?
solution: Thiosulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{HO}-\text{S}(=\text{S})(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$) has one central sulphur atom in $+6$ oxidation state and one terminal sulphur atom in $-2$ oxidation state.

question_text: The oxoacid of phosphorus that is easily obtained from a reaction of alkali and white phosphorus and has two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds, is:
solution: $\text{P}_4 + 3\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{PH}_3 + 3\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2$. Sodium hypophosphite is the salt of phosphinic acid (hypophosphorous acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$), which contains two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds.

question_text: The interhalogen compound formed from the reaction of bromine with excess of fluorine is a:
solution: $\text{Br}_2 + 5\text{F}_2(\text{excess}) \longrightarrow 2\text{BrF}_5$. Upon hydrolysis, $\text{BrF}_5 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{HBrO}_3 + 5\text{HF}$ (bromic acid, a halic(V) acid), so $\text{BrF}_5$ corresponds to a halate.

question_text: Dinitrogen and dioxygen, the main constituents of air, do not react with each other in atmosphere to form oxides of nitrogen because:
options: $\text{N}_2$ is unreactive in the condition of atmosphere.
Reaction between them can occur in the presence of a catalyst.
The reaction is endothermic and requires very high temperature.
solution: The reaction $\text{N}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}(g)$ is strongly endothermic ($\Delta H^\circ = +180.7\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) due to the very high bond dissociation enthalpy of the $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond ($941.4\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) and requires very high temperatures ($\sim 2000\text{ K}$).

question_text: Concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ reacts with iodine to give:
solution: Concentrated nitric acid oxidises iodine to iodic acid: $\text{I}_2 + 10\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc.}) \longrightarrow 2\text{HIO}_3 + 10\text{NO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

question_text: White phosphorus reacts with thionyl chloride to give:
solution: White phosphorus reacts with thionyl chloride to produce phosphorus trichloride, sulphur dioxide, and sulphur monochloride: $\text{P}_4 + 8\text{SOCl}_2 \longrightarrow 4\text{PCl}_3 + 4\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2$.

question_text: Dinitrogen is a robust compound, but reacts at high altitude to form oxides. The oxide of nitrogen that can damage plant leaves and retard photosynthesis is:
solution: Higher concentrations of nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$) damage the leaves of plants, retard the rate of photosynthesis, and act as a respiratory irritant.

question_text: Consider the following sulphur based oxoacids: $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$. Amongst these oxoacids, the number of those with peroxo ($\text{O}-\text{O}$) bond is ______.
solution: Among $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, and $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$, only peroxodisulphuric acid (Marshall's acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$, $\text{HO}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{OH}$) contains a peroxo ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$) linkage ($1$ acid).

question_text: An ammoniacal metal salt solution gives a brilliant red precipitate on addition of dimethylglyoxime. The metal ion is:
solution: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ reacts with dimethylglyoxime ($\text{dmgH}_2$) in ammoniacal medium ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) to form a rosy-red chelate precipitate of bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II), $[\text{Ni}(\text{dmgH})_2]$.

question_text: Which of the phosphorus oxoacids can create silver mirror from $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution?
solution: Oxoacids of phosphorus containing $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds act as strong reducing agents and reduce $\text{AgNO}_3$ to metallic silver (silver mirror). Among the given options, pyrophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$) contains two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds, whereas $(\text{HPO}_3)_n$, $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$, and $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$ have no $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds.

question_text: A chloride salt solution acidified with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ gives a curdy white precipitate, $[\text{A}]$, on addition of $\text{AgNO}_3$. $[\text{A}]$ on treatment with $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ gives a clear solution, $\text{B}$:
solution:

question_text: "$\text{A}$" obtained by Ostwald's method involving air oxidation of $\text{NH}_3$, upon further air oxidation produces "$\text{B}$". "$\text{B}$" on hydration forms an oxoacid of Nitrogen along with evolution of "$\text{A}$". The oxoacid also produces "$\text{A}$" and gives positive brown ring test:
solution: Ostwald's process involves catalytic oxidation of $\text{NH}_3$: $4\text{NH}_3(g) + 5\text{O}_2(g) \xrightarrow{500\text{ K}, 9\text{ bar}} 4\text{NO}(g)[\text{A}] + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$. Nitric oxide combines with oxygen to give $\text{NO}_2$: $2\text{NO}(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2(g)[\text{B}]$. Hydration of $\text{NO}_2$ forms nitric acid: $3\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \longrightarrow 2\text{HNO}_3(aq) + \text{NO}(g)[\text{A}]$. Thus, $\text{A}$ is $\text{NO}$ and $\text{B}$ is $\text{NO}_2$.

question_text: Total number of acidic oxides among $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3, \text{NO}_2, \text{N}_2\text{O}, \text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7, \text{SO}_2, \text{CO}, \text{CaO}, \text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NO}$ is ______.
solution: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{NO}_2$, $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$, and $\text{SO}_2$ are acidic oxides ($4$ oxides); $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, $\text{CO}$, and $\text{NO}$ are neutral oxides; $\text{CaO}$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ are basic oxides.

question_text: Formula for Nessler's reagent is:
solution: Nessler's reagent is an alkaline solution of potassium tetraiodomercurate(II), $\text{K}_2\text{HgI}_4$, used to detect ammonia/ammonium ions (forming a brown precipitate of basic mercury(II) amido-iodide).

question_text: The oxidation state of phosphorus in hypophosphoric acid is ______.
solution: Hypophosphoric acid has the formula $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$. Let the oxidation state of $\text{P}$ be $x$: $4(+1) + 2x + 6(-2) = 0 \implies 2x - 8 = 0 \implies x = +4$.

question_text: When $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion is treated with $\text{KI}$, a white precipitate, $\text{X}$, appears in solution. The solution is titrated with sodium thiosulphate, the compound $\text{Y}$ is formed. $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ respectively are:
solution: $2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{I}^- \longrightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{I}_2\downarrow[\text{X, white ppt.}] + \text{I}_2$. Titration of liberated $\text{I}_2$ with sodium thiosulphate yields sodium tetrathionate: $2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{I}_2 \longrightarrow 2\text{NaI} + \text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6[\text{Y}]$.

Sum of oxidation states of bromine in bromic acid and perbromic acid is ______.
solution: In bromic acid ($\text{HBrO}_3$), oxidation state of $\text{Br}$ is $+5$. In perbromic acid ($\text{HBrO}_4$), oxidation state of $\text{Br}$ is $+7$. Sum $= 5 + 7 = 12$.
